observation.visible_scene: A wide dusk/dawn landscape of a recently burned field under a pale pink, smoke-hazed sky. The foreground is blackened, charred ground dotted with thin standing dead saplings; taller, partly leafless trees stand across the midground and right. Low white smoke hangs over the field. Small active flames burn in two places: a bright patch at the bottom-center foreground and a longer line of fire along the right edge. A 'skyhighnt' watermark sits at the lower right. The view is a static-looking aerial/drone shot that slowly tightens on the scene.
visible_changes: The bottom-center foreground flame gradually shrinks in brightness and size and drifts toward the lower edge, eventually being almost cut out of frame by the end of the clip.
The line of fire on the right edge continues to flicker and smolder throughout, remaining visible at the last frame.
The low smoke layer over the field drifts and shifts subtly in density and position from frame to frame.

The framing slowly tightens (mild zoom-in / slight upward tilt): the central tall tree and the right-side trees grow marginally larger and the bottom foreground content is progressively pushed out of view, while the overall layout of trees and ground stays the same.
The pinkish sky and haze remain essentially constant in color and brightness across the excerpt.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause of the fire and whether it was started before this segment or is spreading beyond the visible edges.
What happens to the foreground flame after it leaves the bottom of the frame (whether it dies out or is simply out of view).
The full extent of the burned area and any activity outside the cropped field of view.
uncertain_details: Whether the apparent tightening is a camera zoom, a slight tilt, or both; the background evidence is too subtle to separate them confidently.
The exact flicker pattern of individual flames is hard to track frame-to-frame; only the overall trend (foreground flame diminishing, right-side fire persisting) is clear.
It is uncertain whether the foreground flame is genuinely weakening or merely being cropped out by the camera movement.
